restatements.text: Parents of children eligible for public school can open an education savings account, into which the state will deposit 90 percent of the per-pupil funds the local public school district would have received for that child.
The funds in the education savings account can be spent on private school tuition, tutoring, textbooks, and approved online courses.

analysis.answer: Currently, state education funds are allocated exclusively to public school districts and charter schools. This measure allows parents to redirect 90% of their child's allocated per-pupil funding into a private education savings account.

The state pays 90% of the per-pupil formula amount into the account, which might represent a 10% per-student savings on students who were already in public schools. However, if students currently paying out-of-pocket for private school or homeschooling become eligible, the state faces significant new direct costs. Compliance costs include the creation and management of the financial accounts and vendor approval systems.

Parents choosing private schooling and tutoring benefit from subsidized costs. Private schools and educational businesses benefit from increased demand. Public school districts bear the cost of reduced funding for every student that opts into the program.

The measure addresses parents' limited financial ability to access alternative educational options by subsidizing private schooling. However, because public schools have fixed operational costs (like building maintenance), losing funding on a per-student basis may create a spillover cost that negatively impacts the students who remain in the district system.

Researchers disagree heavily on the effects of education savings accounts and vouchers. Some find they improve participant outcomes and generate healthy competitive pressure that improves public schools. Others find that participating students often suffer academic learning loss, particularly in math, and that the financial drain harms the public school system.

The availability of state funds will likely increase enrollment at private schools and expand the market for tutors and online educational platforms. Private schools may increase tuition rates in response to the newly available public subsidies.
Parents gain the discretion to direct education spending. Private schools, tutors, and online course providers gain concentrated financial benefits from the newly redirected funds.
Administrative funds will be consumed by managing individual accounts, verifying eligible expenses, preventing fraud, and setting standards for "approved online courses."

flags.note: The text does not specify the criteria for approval or which entity holds the authority to approve these courses.
